1.title: Put white and blue wires in board
1.say: Hold the white board steady, then push the white wire into the top left row. Push the blue wire into the top right row.
placements: white power wire → upper field left side in its own five-hole row, pushed by hand until firm and standing upright to the left of the blue wire (in the video: top edge left side, printed numbers not readable, about 3 holes from left edge)

blue power wire → upper field right side in its own five-hole row separate from the white wire, pushed by hand until firm and standing upright to the right of the white wire (in the video: top edge right side, printed numbers not readable, about 2 holes from right edge)
watch_for: If both wires share the same five-hole row the batteries are shorted, so leave several empty holes between them.
If a wire wobbles or falls out it is too loose, so push it deeper until it stands firm.
1.check_yourself: It should look like the white board sits on the table with a white wire and a blue wire standing up from its top edge.

2.title: Put resistor across the board
2.say: Push one leg of the blue resistor into the white wire row. Push the other leg into an empty row a few holes to the right.
placements: small blue banded resistor with two thin wire legs → left leg in same five-hole row as white power wire on the left, right leg in empty five-hole row a few holes to the right, body lying flat across the top, pushed by hand (in the video: across top band spanning about 4 to 5 holes, printed numbers not readable)
watch_for: If both legs sit in the same five-hole row the resistor does nothing, so check the legs are a few holes apart.
If the light later stays dark a leg may miss its row, so reseat each leg fully into its row.
2.check_yourself: It should look like a small blue banded resistor lies flat across the top of the white board.

3.title: Plug in the blue LED
3.say: Push the short leg of the blue LED into the resistor row. Push the long leg into the blue wire row.
placements: round blue LED with long plus leg and short minus leg with flat side → short leg in same five-hole row as resistor right leg on the right side, long leg in same five-hole row as blue power wire on the right side, pushed by hand until standing upright on the top right (in the video: top edge right corner, long leg to the right by the blue wire, short leg to the left by the resistor, lights blue when powered)
watch_for: If the blue light stays dark the long and short legs are probably swapped, so switch the two holes.
If both legs share the same five-hole row the light will stay dark, so keep them in separate rows.
3.check_yourself: It should look like the blue LED stands upright on the white board glowing blue.
